title: Reduce CPU-side contention and serialization overhead in request path
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: production traces from perf-canary and customer Dedicated clusters showed that a non-trivial fraction of tail latency and CPU utilization is spent on CPU-side request plumbing: JSON serialization/deserialization for control frames, shared thread-pool contention, and hotspots around KV cache lookup locks. This PR optimizes the request path to reduce overhead and contention without changing the public API. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a compact binary frame for intra-service control messages to replace verbose JSON in hot code paths; frames are backward compatible and negotiated per-connection. 2) Replace the global thread-pool used for small async tasks with per-core worker pools pinned to CPU cores on Linux and macOS where supported; use an efficient MPMC handoff for cross-core work. 3) Change KV cache from a single sharded lock to per-shard lock-free read paths using sequence counters and an RCU-style updater to avoid short-lived lock contention during heavy read bursts. 4) Move metadata serialization off the hot path by preserializing common route headers and attaching by reference when request creation occurs. 5) Add a lightweight request-affinity scheduler that prefers placing related short-lived requests on the same core to improve KV cache locality and reduce cache misses. Testing and validation: unit and integration tests updated for frame negotiation and thread-pinning config. Added deterministic stress tests that simulate 5k concurrent small requests to validate no regressions in correctness. Perf results (perf-canary synthetic workload matching our microburst profile): median latency unchanged, p95 latency reduced by ~18-22% on typical CPU-heavy workloads, CPU sys usage down ~28% on 8-core instances in our lab, average throughput improved ~12% under load, and instance-level tail jitter reduced. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag "cpu_optimizations_v1" and enabled via a canary rollout to 5% of dedicated pools; observed metrics and rollback hooks added to console. Checklist: - [x] Design and perf prototypes - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf canary results - [x] Documentation update in docs/perf.md - [x] Rollout gating and console integration

review_thread: Marcus Li: Strong improvement in the perf numbers. Two main asks: 1) can we make the frame negotiation opt-in at connection start so older clients don't get unexpected behavior? 2) add a brief doc about how to audit the per-core pinning in production.

Author (Aisha Patel): Addressed both. Frame negotiation is implemented with a connection-level capability bit and falls back to JSON. Added docs/perf.md section on pinning observability and added a runtime flag to disable pinning per-process.
Diego Ramos: Noted a potential live-upgrade concern for the KV cache RCU updater; requested an additional stress test simulating concurrent readers during chest operations.
Author: Added deterministic stress test that runs concurrent readers/writers with epoch rollover; results attached to perf-canary logs. No data corruption seen; latency stable.
Priya Nair: Approved after verifying CI and canary traces. Left a minor nits comment about naming in thread_pool.rs, fixed in follow-up commit.
Marcus Li: Approved and requested merge when perf-canary finishes a second clean run in staging.
release_notes: Reduced tail latency by optimizing CPU-side request path: binary control frames, per-core pinned worker pools, lock-free KV cache reads, pre-serialized metadata, and request-affinity scheduler. Feature gated behind cpu_optimizations_v1. No API changes expected.
summary_benchmarks: tail jitter: reduced 30% measured by 99th percentile across canary hosts
rationale: Hot-path CPU work was dominated by small allocations, JSON framing, and lock contention. Addressing these structural issues yields consistent p95 improvements for short requests which are a large portion of our customer workloads. The changes are gated and have observability to rollback if needed.
